title: Azure Compute

header.html: Compare compute types, including containers, virtual machines, and functions; Describe virtual machine options, including Azure virtual machines, Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets, availability sets, and Azure Virtual Desktop; Describe the resources required for virtual machines; Describe application hosting options, including web apps, containers, and virtual machines
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

html:
1Compute types compared

Type What it is You manage Best for
Virtual machines Emulated computers that run an operating system (IaaS) OS, patches, software, scaling Full control, lift and shift, custom software
Containers Lightweight packages of an app with what it needs, sharing the host OS The app image (and orchestration if used) Microservices, fast start, portable apps
Functions (serverless) Small pieces of code that run on events Only the code Event-driven tasks, automation, pay per run

Exam tip

. More control = more to manage. VMs are the most control, functions the least. A container is lighter than a VM because it does not include a full operating system.

2Virtual machines (Azure Virtual Machines)

Azure Virtual Machines give you a server you control (IaaS). You choose the size, operating system (Windows or Linux) and software.

Use VMs when you need total control of the OS, run custom or legacy software, or do a lift and shift. You are responsible for patching and maintenance of the guest OS.

VM options

Option What it does
Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets Create and manage a group of identical, load-balanced VMs; the number of instances can grow or shrink automatically with demand or a schedule
Availability sets Spread VMs across fault domains (separate hardware, power, network) and update domains (groups rebooted together during maintenance) inside one datacenter, so one failure or update does not take all VMs down
Availability zones (Module 4) Place VMs in separate datacenters of a region for stronger protection
Azure Virtual Desktop A desktop and app virtualization service in the cloud: users reach a Windows desktop from nearly any device
Exam tip

. Scale set = identical VMs, autoscale. Availability set = protect from hardware failure and planned maintenance within a datacenter. Azure Virtual Desktop = remote desktops delivered from Azure. Zones are better than sets for datacenter-level failure.

Resources a VM needs

A VM is not just the machine. Creating one usually involves:

Resource Purpose
Compute (the VM itself: size, CPU, memory) Runs the OS and apps
Storage (OS disk, optional data disks) Holds the operating system and data
Networking (virtual network, subnet, network interface) Connects the VM
Public IP address (optional) Reach the VM from the internet
Network security group (optional but common) Filters traffic with rules

3Containers

A container packages an application and its dependencies and shares the host operating system, so it starts faster and uses fewer resources than a VM.

Azure service What it does
Azure Container Instances (ACI) Run a container quickly without managing VMs or an orchestrator; good for simple apps and short jobs
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) A managed Kubernetes service to deploy, scale and manage many containers (orchestration)
Azure Container Apps Beyond the study guide Serverless containers for microservices without managing Kubernetes
Exam tip

. One or a few containers, no orchestration → ACI. Many containers, orchestration, scaling → AKS.

4Azure Functions

Azure Functions is serverless: you write code that runs when an event (trigger) happens, such as an HTTP request, a timer or a new file. Azure scales it automatically and, on the consumption model, you pay only while it runs.

Use it for small, event-driven tasks, such as processing an uploaded file or running a job on a schedule.

5Application hosting options

Option Type Use it when
Azure App Service (web apps) PaaS You build web apps, APIs and mobile back ends and do not want to manage servers. It supports several languages and gives built-in scaling and deployment
Containers (ACI, AKS) Containers The app is packaged as containers or built as microservices
Virtual machines IaaS You need full OS control or must run custom software
Azure Functions Serverless The code is event driven and short

Choose: web app, no server work → App Service; packaged app → containers; special software or legacy server → VM; event-triggered snippets → Functions.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants a group of identical web servers that adds instances automatically when traffic rises. Which service fits?

  • AAvailability set
  • BAzure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
  • CAzure Container Instances
  • DAzure Virtual Desktop
Show the answer

Answer: B. Scale sets manage identical, load-balanced VMs and can autoscale. An availability set only spreads VMs across fault and update domains.

S2A team wants to run a single container quickly without managing servers or an orchestrator. Which service fits?

  • AAzure Kubernetes Service
  • BAzure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
  • CAzure Container Instances
  • DAzure Virtual Desktop
Show the answer

Answer: C. ACI runs containers without VM or orchestrator management. AKS is for orchestrating many containers.

S3A developer wants to host a web app without managing the operating system. Which option fits best?

  • AAzure App Service
  • BAzure Virtual Machines
  • CAn availability set
  • DA private cloud
Show the answer

Answer: A. App Service is a PaaS offering for web apps and APIs.

S4Which resources does a typical Azure virtual machine need in addition to compute?

  • AStorage and networking
  • BA management group
  • CA sovereign region
  • DA resource lock
Show the answer

Answer: A. A VM needs storage for its disks and networking (virtual network and interface), with optional public IP and network security group.

S5Employees need to use a Windows desktop hosted in Azure from any device. Which service fits?

  • AAzure Functions
  • BAzure Virtual Desktop
  • CAzure Policy
  • DAzure Container Apps
Show the answer

Answer: B. Azure Virtual Desktop delivers desktops and apps from the cloud.

S6Code must run only when a new file arrives, and the company wants to pay only while it runs. Which compute type fits?

  • AVirtual machine
  • BAvailability set
  • CAKS node pool
  • DAzure Functions
Show the answer

Answer: D. Functions are event-driven serverless code billed for execution.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which compute type gives the most control?

Show the answer

Virtual machines.

R2Why is a container lighter than a VM?

Show the answer

It shares the host operating system instead of including a full one.

R3What is the difference between a scale set and an availability set?

Show the answer

A scale set manages identical VMs that autoscale; an availability set spreads VMs over fault and update domains in one datacenter.

R4Which service orchestrates many containers?

Show the answer

Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

R5What starts an Azure function?

Show the answer

A trigger (event), such as HTTP, a timer or a new file.

R6Which hosting option is PaaS for web apps?

Show the answer

Azure App Service.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
VMs IaaS; full control; you patch the OS; lift and shift
Scale Sets identical VMs, load balanced, autoscale
Availability set fault and update domains in one datacenter; zones are stronger
Azure Virtual Desktop cloud desktops and apps for users
VM resources compute, storage (disks), networking, optional public IP and NSG
Containers share host OS; ACI = quick and simple; AKS = orchestration
Functions serverless, event triggers, pay per execution
App Service PaaS for web apps and APIs
